title: Label-free mitochondrial imaging distinguishes perturbed retinal-cell states
summary: AutoMitoNetwork combined learned image segmentation and support vector classification to analyze label-free mitochondrial images from a human retinal-cell line. Across 62 control, 65 respiration-inhibited and 62 glycolysis-inhibited cells, the study measured treatment-associated network changes and distinguished subtler perturbed states using combined image features. Cell-level train/test separation supported the bounded in-vitro finding; this does not establish a new causal mechanism, disease diagnosis or patient benefit.

source_review.scope: Primary full article Methods, Results and limitations plus Europe PMC bibliographic metadata; indexed primary publisher full text.

evidence.tested: New in-vitro retinal-cell image measurements and cell-separated classification of perturbation-linked states.
evidence.unknown: Disease diagnostic performance, independent laboratory replication and new causal mechanisms remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Ilastik learned segmentation enables feature extraction; PCA/LDA transform training features and linear SVM classifies cell-separated test sets. Newly measured treated-cell network states rather than software availability alone support admission.
